**Analyzing physical separation**

I'm noticing that these objects don't physically share an edge since they are separated by a wall. So, they exist in the same section but remain disconnected. Although they have opposing shell surfaces, there's no adjacency. I wonder if I should categorize them as a disconnected subgroup. But then again, maybe the sections should be classified as shells, and the adjacency list could reflect two subgroups without specific notation. It's a bit confusing!
**Considering structural relationships**

I'm analyzing the structure of the cavity, specifically the FACE6 model. I see there are relationships within each section; the outer might have two parts, while the cavity and rim could also have two each. I think getting a clear layout of these connections will be important for fully understanding the system. It feels a bit complex, but I want to make sure I’m capturing all the nuanced relationships correctly!

part.name: Hollow saddle cradle support
part.description: A rectangular, open-bottom support shell with a longitudinal concave cylindrical cradle surface, short planar end lands, thick lateral and end walls, and a recessed underside cavity. The outer envelope is 2.0 mm wide by 6.0 mm long by 1.5 mm high. No holes, fasteners, discrete joints, or other mounting points are present.
part.symmetry_note: The part is bilaterally symmetric about the x=0 longitudinal center plane and end-for-end symmetric about the y=0 transverse plane. It is not symmetric about the horizontal z=0 plane because the upper cradle and open underside cavity perform different functions.

Section.name: Outer cradle shell
Section.function intent: Provides the primary supporting and locating interface for a long cylindrical or rounded mating component while carrying the resulting load into the side and end walls.
Section.physical behavior: The concave cylindrical surface distributes contact pressure over a broad area and constrains lateral movement of a mating cylinder. The side and end walls resist bending and shear, maintain the cradle profile, and transfer loads toward the bottom perimeter.
Section.geometry: The exterior consists of a radius 4.215 mm cylindrical trough with its axis parallel to the x direction, bounded along y by short horizontal lands at z=0.75 mm. Planar side walls at x=-1.0 mm and x=1.0 mm follow the saddle profile, while planar end walls at y=-3.0 mm and y=3.0 mm close the outer envelope.
Section.location: Exterior and upper portion of the part, surrounding the cavity on both lateral sides and both longitudinal ends.

major_faces.name: Negative-y outer end wall
major_faces.description: Planar rectangular end face at y=-3.0 mm spanning the full 2.0 mm width and 1.5 mm overall height.

major_faces.name: Negative-y top land
major_faces.description: Horizontal planar land at z=0.75 mm between the negative-y end wall and the start of the outer cylindrical cradle.

major_faces.name: Negative-x outer side wall
major_faces.description: Planar longitudinal side face at x=-1.0 mm with a saddle-shaped upper boundary.

major_faces.name: Outer cylindrical cradle
major_faces.description: Primary concave cylindrical support surface of radius 4.215 mm, extending across the full 2.0 mm outer width.

major_faces.name: Positive-x outer side wall
major_faces.description: Planar longitudinal side face at x=1.0 mm, symmetric to the negative-x outer side wall.

major_faces.name: Positive-y outer end wall
major_faces.description: Planar rectangular end face at y=3.0 mm spanning the full width and height of the outer envelope.

major_faces.name: Positive-y top land
major_faces.description: Horizontal planar land at z=0.75 mm between the positive-y end wall and the outer cylindrical cradle.

relationships.function relationship: distributes_stress; provides the load-bearing exterior while maintaining clearance for the underside cavity
relationships.structural relationship: offset_from; attached_to; the outer and inner cylindrical surfaces form opposing boundaries of the same thin shell

relationships.function relationship: transmits_load; transfers cradle and wall loads into the bottom perimeter rim
relationships.structural relationship: attached_to; blends_into; the external side and end walls terminate continuously at the bottom rim

Section.name: Underside cavity
features included: Nominal 0.2 mm shell offsets from the outer walls and cradle
Section.function intent: Removes nonessential material while retaining a shell of approximately uniform thickness beneath the cradle and around the perimeter. It also provides underside clearance for adjacent structure or manufacturing access.
Section.physical behavior: The cavity reduces mass and material usage. Its inner cylindrical ceiling follows the outer cradle with a larger radius, maintaining approximately 0.2 mm normal thickness through the curved region. The inner side and end walls preserve a perimeter box section that improves bending stiffness relative to a completely flat thin sheet.
Section.geometry: A rectangular open-bottom recess bounded by internal side walls at x=-0.8 mm and x=0.8 mm and internal end walls at y=-2.8 mm and y=2.8 mm. Its ceiling comprises a radius 4.415 mm cylindrical surface centered on the same x-axis as the outer cradle, plus short planar end patches at z=0.55 mm.
Section.location: Inside the lower portion of the part, opening through the bottom and enclosed laterally by the outer shell and bottom rim.

major_faces.name: Negative-y cavity end wall
major_faces.description: Internal planar transverse wall at y=-2.8 mm closing the negative-y end of the underside cavity.

major_faces.name: Negative-y inner ceiling land
major_faces.description: Small horizontal cavity-ceiling patch at z=0.55 mm adjoining the negative-y cavity end wall and inner cylinder.

major_faces.name: Positive-x cavity side wall
major_faces.description: Internal planar longitudinal wall at x=0.8 mm following the underside saddle profile.

major_faces.name: Inner cylindrical cavity ceiling
major_faces.description: Cylindrical underside surface of radius 4.415 mm, coaxial with and offset below the outer cradle surface.

major_faces.name: Negative-x cavity side wall
major_faces.description: Internal planar longitudinal wall at x=-0.8 mm, symmetric to the positive-x cavity side wall.

major_faces.name: Positive-y inner ceiling land
major_faces.description: Small horizontal cavity-ceiling patch at z=0.55 mm adjoining the inner cylinder and positive-y cavity end wall.

major_faces.name: Positive-y cavity end wall
major_faces.description: Internal planar transverse wall at y=2.8 mm closing the positive-y end of the underside cavity.

relationships.function relationship: provides_clearance; reduces mass while preserving the load-supporting outer cradle
provides_clearance; the cavity opening is defined and reinforced by the perimeter rim
relationships.structural relationship: adjacent_to; contained_in; the internal side and end walls terminate at the inner boundary of the rim

Section.name: Bottom perimeter rim
features included: Tie between inner and outer wall systems
Section.function intent: Provides a flat base or bearing perimeter, reinforces the open cavity mouth, and ties the inner cavity walls to the external walls.
Section.physical behavior: The continuous planar frame distributes compressive reaction loads around the perimeter and limits spreading or distortion of the thin side and end walls. Its central opening preserves access to the cavity and avoids unnecessary material.
Section.geometry: A planar rectangular frame at z=-0.75 mm with an outer boundary of 2.0 mm by 6.0 mm and an inner cavity opening approximately 1.6 mm by 5.6 mm. The STEP face contains two wires corresponding to the outer perimeter and inner opening.
Section.location: Lowest surface of the part, surrounding the open underside cavity.

major_faces.name: Bottom rectangular rim
major_faces.description: Flat annular rectangular face at z=-0.75 mm connecting the external walls to the internal cavity walls.

relationships.function relationship: provides_clearance; constrains_dof of the cavity-wall edges against lateral spreading
